rows: Think of a kitchen. Change one ingredient and the whole thing moves. What is your ingredient?
Brawling is like salt. A little is useful. Too much spoils the whole dish.
A risk is like a dodgy shelf. It might hold, but I would not put my weight on it.
Slow is like a long simmer. It takes patience, and I enjoy it.
The people are the ones who eat the meal. They should get something they enjoy.
Short version: I have made the dish, and I know what it tastes like.
I am not the loudest thing in the kitchen, but I know my recipe.
Look at my stance. It is the way I chop the vegetables: carefully.
You say technique. Which ingredient do you rely on when the dish goes wrong?
Strikes are the heat. Too much and everything burns. Where do you stop?
A risk without a fallback is like cooking without a timer. Who is watching it?
A stall is a dish left on the side. Nobody gets fed.
The people have a right to a dish they understand. Let me show you the recipe.
You call yourself among the best. Let us taste it and see.
You are proud of your {strength}. That is a good ingredient. I know exactly what to do with it.
I have tasted your {strength} twice. It is good, but it needs a pinch of something else.
You kept calm. Good. It keeps the pan from boiling over.
Fair. We agree on the first ingredient, which is a start.
I could tell you what I think of the recipe. I would rather let you taste it.
One fall. Clean recipe, clear result. Keep me down and I will say the dish was good.
On the mat, every step is a stir. Keep up with me.
Grounded or standing, the recipe still starts with the first grip.
Stay in front of me and show me your next ingredient.
Good answer. It is well seasoned.
You have not answered. The dish is going cold.
Fair. I will take that ingredient on board.
I accept that. It is a fair place to start the dish.
I will cook this match slowly and finish it properly.
My approach is gentle and steady. I will show you the method.
Whatever happens, you will know what went into it.
The dish is not ready yet. One more ingredient to add.
I have one more ingredient in mind. You will taste it when the bell rings.
